ai.title: Move DynamicAgentService and AgentTemplate to common
ai.summary: Relocated `DynamicAgentService` and `AgentTemplate` types from `backend` to `common` to decouple shared logic. `backend/src/templates/types.ts` now re-exports these definitions from `@codebuff/common` for backward compatibility. This change affects `backend/src/templates/agent-registry.ts` and introduces `common/src/types/agent-template.ts`.

eli5.text: The pieces that define how custom agents are built and run have been moved from the backend into the shared 'common' area, so both the backend and any other code that relies on these shared definitions now pull them from one central place. As a result, the backend no longer ships its own copy of these types and instead imports them from common, while its old local reference point now quietly forwards requests to the new home so existing code keeps working. You wouldn't see a visible difference in behavior, but the system is now organized so future features built on these shared agent-building blocks will be easier to maintain and less likely to break.

ai.title: DynamicAgentConfigSchema enforces lowercase-hyphen agent ID regex
ai.summary: DynamicAgentConfigSchema in common/src/types/dynamic-agent-template.ts now validates agent id against /^[a-z0-9-]+$/, rejecting uppercase letters. agent-config.d.ts JSDoc updated to match. Covers shared core types consumed by CLI, Web, and Desktop. Existing agents with uppercase IDs fail validation on load.

eli5.text: Starting today, agent IDs must now use only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens (like 'my-agent-2'). If any existing agent has an uppercase letter in its ID, it will be rejected and fail to load. This rule is now enforced across the shared core system used by the CLI, web, and desktop apps.

ai.title: Refactor eval runner control flow and add analysis timeout
ai.summary: Refactored `runEvalSet` in `run-eval-set.ts` to move post-eval analysis out of the try/catch block, ensuring eval duration is logged consistently regardless of analysis success. Added a 10-minute timeout to the `analyzeEvalResults` call in `post-eval-analysis.ts` to prevent hanging on large traces. Applied minor formatting fixes to prompt construction and trace truncation logic in `judge-git-eval.ts`.

eli5.text: You wouldn't see a difference in how the evaluation runs, but if a run happened to hang during its analysis stage, it now gives up after ten minutes instead of waiting forever. Behind the scenes, the team shuffled around some order of operations so that how long the evaluation itself took gets printed out reliably, even if the later analysis part fails. A few extra spaces and blank lines were tidied up in the files that prepare the text prompts, which has no effect on what you see but makes the code easier to read. These changes are already in place today.

ai.title: Use local .bin/bun in fileChangeHooks test commands
ai.summary: The `backend-unit-tests`, `npm-app-unit-tests`, and `common-unit-tests` fileChangeHooks in `codebuff.json` now invoke `../.bin/bun test` instead of relying on the global `bun` command. This change ensures tests run against the repository's pinned Bun version, preventing failures caused by environment discrepancies. The scope is limited to `codebuff.json` and affects local development and CI hook execution for `backend`, `npm-app`, and `common` packages.

eli5.text: When you save a code file, the tools that run your tests now use the exact testing software version your project keeps in its own folder, rather than whatever version happens to be installed on your machine. This means your tests will behave the same way on your computer, your teammate's computer, and in the automated testing service the project uses. If you look at your terminal while these tests run, you won't see any difference in the output what you see is still the list of things that passed or failed but you are now protected from the situation where a test passes for you locally but fails somewhere else just because of a software version mismatch.

ai.title: Add agent publish flag and API routes
ai.summary: Introduces a --publish flag that uploads a local agent template from .agents to the agent store via handlePublish and a POST /api/agents/publish route, alongside GET routes resolving agents by version and latest. The schema renames agent_template to agent_config and drops the slug/unique constraint in favor of a user_id foreign key, while version-utils provides parseVersion, incrementPatchVersion, getLatestAgentVersion, determineNextVersion, and versionExists consumed by the publish endpoint. This wires up the store schema and CLI entry point so publishers can push templates end to end.
ai.evidence: Added `--publish <agent-name>` flag to cliOptions in npm-app/src/cli-definitions.ts with handler branch in npm-app/src/index.ts calling handlePublish from npm-app/src/cli-handlers/publish.ts; added three Next.js route handlers under web/src/app/api/agents for publishing and retrieving agent configs; added publisher.ts type defs, version-utils.ts helpers, and schema.ts agent_config/publisher changes.
ai.unknowns: The README or web UI for publisher profile management referenced in later commits is not present here, and the consumer that reads the GET route responses is not visible yet.

changes.what: Added --publish CLI flag wired to handlePublish in a new cli-handlers/publish.ts module that loads local agents and POSTs to the publish endpoint.
Added POST /api/agents/publish and GET routes under web/src/app/api/agents to publish and fetch agent configs by version and latest.
Renamed agent_template table and slug column to agent_config and added a user_id foreign key on publisher per the new schema and migration 0026_chilly_mockingbird.sql.
Added version-utils with parseVersion, incrementPatchVersion, getLatestAgentVersion, determineNextVersion, and versionExists re-exported from packages/internal/src/index.ts.
Added PublisherIdSchema, PublisherSchema, and PublisherInput validation schemas to a new publisher.ts module.

ai.title: Fix pgstatstatements drop error in Drizzle config
ai.summary: Added tablesFilter to common/src/db/drizzle.config.ts to exclude pg_stat_statements and pg_stat_statements_info from migrations. This prevents "cannot drop view pg_stat_statements_info because extension pg_stat_statements requires it" errors during schema sync. Also updated .agents/agent-config.d.ts to enforce lowercase, numeric, and hyphen-only constraints for agent IDs.

eli5.text: You: When you ask your workspace to reset a database extension that tracks usage statistics, it no longer tries to remove two built-in tracking views that the extension itself depends on, so the reset completes instead of stopping with an error. The fix works by telling the database setup step which table-like objects to leave alone during a reset. It's live now.

ai.title: Allow empty system prompt in runAgentStep
ai.summary: runAgentStep now defaults system prompt to empty string instead of throwing on missing prompt. getAgentPrompt result uses nullish coalescing operator. Removes hard requirement for system prompt in backend/src/run-agent-step.ts.

eli5.text: The assistant can now run steps even when no special instructions are given to it beforehand, instead of stopping and complaining that instructions are missing. Behind the scenes, the system now treats a missing instruction as simply blank rather than an error, so automated agents that previously had to supply instructions will no longer break if they leave that field empty.

ai.title: CLI: publish flag becomes subcommand
ai.summary: The `--publish` CLI flag is removed from `cliOptions` in `npm-app/src/cli-definitions.ts` and replaced with a `publish` subcommand handled in `npm-app/src/index.ts`. The parser now checks `args[0] === 'publish'` instead of `options.publish`, extracting the agent name from `args[1]`. This change prevents the publish argument from being incorrectly parsed as initial user input by adding an `isCommand` guard before setting `initialInput`. Scope limited to CLI entry point and definition files.

eli5.text: The way you tell the tool to publish an agent has changed: instead of typing a special --publish option before the agent name, you now type 'publish' as a verb first. For example, you would change from running the command with '--publish my-agent' to running it as 'publish my-agent'. This affects only the small group of people who use the publish command, and it fixes a quirk where the agent name could mistakenly be treated as the first thing you asked the tool to do. The new approach is live today.

ai.title: publish loads credentials directly
ai.summary: CLI publish handler now reads auth tokens via new getUserCredentials helper instead of Client singleton. Eliminates client initialization dependency for this command. Covers npm-app/src/cli-handlers/publish.ts and npm-app/src/credentials.ts. Parameter renamed agentName to agentId to match template lookup logic.

eli5.text: When you run the publish command to upload your agent template, the tool now reads your login credentials straight from the local credentials file instead of going through a shared client module first. This means the publish command no longer depends on the client being initialized beforehand, and the parameter you pass is referred to as the agent's id rather than its name to match how templates are looked up. If you run publish without being logged in, you'll still see the same "please log in first" message, but the underlying check is now simpler and more direct.

ai.title: Remove loadFileContents from agent loader
ai.summary: Removed `loadFileContents` from `npm-app/src/agents/agent-utils.ts` and its usage in `load-agents.ts`. Prompt fields (`systemPrompt`, `instructionsPrompt`, `stepPrompt`) now pass through directly or default to empty strings instead of resolving file paths. This simplifies the agent loading mechanism by eliminating redundant filesystem lookups for prompt content.

eli5.text: When the system loads assistant definitions, it no longer tries to follow file-path references to fill in the AI instructions text; instead, any instructions typed directly into the definition are used as-is, and if none are present they stay blank. This only affects how internal assistant configurations are assembled behind the scenes, so you won't notice any new buttons or behaviors when using the product.

ai.title: Update ESLint and Prettier config for import rules
ai.summary: ESLint config now enforces import ordering with 'type' group and flags unused imports via eslint-plugin-unused-imports. Prettier trailingComma set to 'all'. VS Code save action changed from organizeImports to fixAll.eslint. npm-app src import restriction removed.

eli5.text: Your editor now automatically cleans up and sorts your code imports for you whenever you save a file, instead of just rearranging them after you ask. While you type, it will also underline any imports you are no longer using so you can delete them, and every line of code in the project will carry a small comma at the end of lists that previously stopped just short of the last item. This only affects people writing code in this project, and the cleanup happens silently as you work.

ai.title: Add eslint-plugin-unused-imports dev dependency
ai.summary: Added eslint-plugin-unused-imports ^4.1.4 to devDependencies in package.json. Provides linting rules for detecting and removing unused imports. Internal tooling change only, no runtime impact.

eli5.text: This is a behind-the-scenes change that only affects how the code is checked for quality. It adds a tool that scans for and flags parts of the code that aren’t actually being used, helping keep the project clean and efficient. You wouldn’t notice anything different unless you’re looking at the developer tools; the app itself behaves exactly the same.

ai.title: Refactor run-agent-step.ts: type-only imports and trailing commas
ai.summary: backend/src/run-agent-step.ts updated to use `import type` for type-only symbols (AgentRegistry, AgentResponseTrace, etc.) and added trailing commas to function arguments. This aligns with TypeScript best practices for tree-shaking and code style consistency. Scope limited to backend agent execution logic.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the part of the system that runs each turn of an AI assistant was cleaned up so it only carries the pieces of instructions it actually needs to run, dropping the rest until they're requested. This is purely maintenance work inside the backend agent logic, so you won't see any change in how the AI behaves or responds today.

ai.title: Publisher profile system and agent publishing CLI
ai.summary: Added publisher profile management via new web routes (`/api/publishers`, `/api/upload/avatar`) and UI pages for creating/editing profiles. CLI `publish` command updated to send structured validation errors and stack traces, replacing generic logger calls that masked errors. Shared types `Publisher`, `CreatePublisherRequest`, and `PublisherProfileResponse` added to `common`. Avatar uploads stored in `web/public/uploads/`, now gitignored. Project root initialization moved to `initializeProjectRootAndWorkingDir` helper in `npm-app`.

eli5.text: When you go to publish an agent through the command line, the program now tells you exactly what went wrong if something failsâlike pointing to the specific spot in your settings that needs fixing instead of giving a vague error message. At the same time, you can now create and manage a publisher profile through a new section of the website, where you can set a name, add a short bio, and upload a profile picture that gets saved to the site's image folder. This profile system is live for anyone using the web interface to create or edit profiles, and the improved error reporting is active for anyone running publish commands from the command line.

ai.title: Inject TOOLSPROMPT into agent system prompts
ai.summary: getAgentPrompt now appends PLACEHOLDER.TOOLS_PROMPT to systemPrompt strings in backend/src/templates/strings.ts. If the placeholder is absent, it is concatenated with a double newline; if the prompt is undefined, it defaults to the placeholder. This ensures tool instructions are always present in the final formatted prompt. Refactor also groups type imports and adds trailing commas.

eli5.text: The instructions that tell each assistant how to use its tools are now automatically attached to every system prompt, even when a specific prompt was missing that attachment before. If you are running an internal agent workflow, the assistant will now consistently receive the guidance it needs to call its tools rather than sometimes missing it. When you looked at the prompt that gets sent to the model, you would now see the tool-usage guidance appended as its own block of text.

ai.title: Add @AgentName spawn directive to base prompt
ai.summary: Added instruction to `backend/src/templates/base-prompts.ts` requiring agent spawning when users mention `@AgentName`. This ensures the model respects explicit user requests to invoke specific sub-agents. Scope limited to backend prompt templates. The directive mandates spawning all mentioned agents.

eli5.text: When you tag a specific helper by name (for example, typing '@Researcher') in a request, the system will now automatically summon that exact helper to join the task, instead of guessing which helpers might be useful. Previously, the system chose helpers on its own, so your named request could be overlooked. You'd notice that any helper you explicitly mention now reliably shows up to assist. This applies to everyone who can request help from these specialized assistants today.

ai.title: agent-builder injects tool definitions
ai.summary: agent-builder.ts now calls compileToolDefinitions() during template construction. Injects 'Available Tools Type Definitions' section into prompt context alongside existing agent types. Refactors tool definition compilation from execution step to initialization scope.

eli5.text: If you asked the agent-builder to create or edit an agent type, its written instructions now include a full list of every tool that agents can use, not just the type definitions for the agent structure itself. The agent gets this tool list when its instructions are first put together, instead of waiting until it actually runs a command. The result: the builder has more complete reference material to work from when you ask it to build you a custom agent.

ai.title: stepPrompt optional in agent config schema
ai.summary: stepPrompt field changed from required to optional in DynamicAgentConfigSchema and AgentConfig interface. Reflected in common/src/types/dynamic-agent-template.ts and common/src/util/agent-config.d.ts. Allows agent configs to omit stepPrompt when not needed for specific model behaviors.

eli5.text: The step-by-step instruction that tells the assistant how to behave during each task is no longer a required field in agent configurations. Anyone setting up an agent configuration can now leave it out when it isn't needed, especially for advanced models that already follow instructions well. This gives developers more flexibility when building custom agent behaviors.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.446
ai.summary: Package version updated to 1.0.446 in npm-app/release/package.json. Internal release metadata change.

eli5.text: A new bundle of capabilities went live for anyone running the assistant on July 30, 2025. Agents can now be published directly from the command line, which means creators can register themselves as publishers, attach their AI agents, and make them available to others, all through a new publishing command in the terminal. The publishing flow now reads your login credentials directly instead of relying on a shared connection object, so your auth is handled more securely per session. Along with publishing, agent configuration files now enforce stricter naming rules (lowercase with hyphens), the placeholder used to inject tool instructions into an agent's system prompt is now being included, and step prompts have become optional, so incomplete setup files won't block agent creation. Behind the scenes, the system moved shared agent-building pieces into a common area, updated the database schema to better track publishers and agent templates, added a tool to auto-generate type definitions for building agents visually, and switched test commands to use the locally installed test runner. If you looked at your installed assistant, it would simply report version 1.0.446, with all these capabilities now active and ready to use.

ai.title: Refactor version handling to structured object
ai.summary: Version logic in `packages/internal` shifts from string parsing to a structured `Version` object with `major`, `minor`, `patch` fields. `getLatestAgentVersion` now returns a `Version` object instead of a string or null, defaulting to `{ major: 0, minor: 0, patch: 0 }` if no version exists. The `web/src/app/api/agents/publish/route.ts` consumer updates to accept the `Version` type and uses `stringifyVersion` before inserting into the database. This internal refactor improves type safety and comparison logic via `getMaximumVersion`.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the system that tracks assistant versions switched from storing them as plain text strings to using neatly separated version numbers (major, minor, patch). This makes comparing versions and automatically incrementing them more reliable, so when one gets published the correct next version number is picked without mistakes. If you look at the publish workflow now it accepts these structured version numbers and converts them back to the familiar format like '1.2.3' before saving. The tooling flagged it notable because the old string-based logic was causing incorrect version bumps.

ai.title: Remove unused version regex constant
ai.summary: Removed the unused `versionRegex` constant from `packages/internal/src/utils/version-utils.ts`. This change cleans up dead code in the internal utils package. No functional impact on version parsing or agent version determination logic.

eli5.text: The team removed a leftover rule used for checking version numbers that nothing in the system was actually using anymore. It does not change how versions are read, parsed, or picked behind the scenes, so you would not notice any difference in behavior. This is the kind of cleanup developers do to keep the internal code tidy, and it only affects the internal tooling package used by the system.

ai.title: agent-builder move types into .agents/types subdirectory
ai.summary: agent-builder.ts relocates agent type definitions from the root `.agents` directory to `.agents/types`. `TEMPLATE_TYPES_PATH` and `TOOL_DEFINITIONS_PATH` now resolve against `TYPES_DIR`, and the `mkdir` command targets this new subdirectory. Generated agent templates must import `AgentConfig` from `./types/agent-config`. Updates prompt instructions and file path constants in `backend/src/templates/agents/agent-builder.ts`.

eli5.text: The system now stores agent type definitions in a new 'types' folder under the main agents directory instead of directly in the agents folder. This affects how generated agent templates are structured and where they import their configuration from. If you looked at the generated templates, you would see they now begin by importing their configuration from the new types location, and the system commands that create these files now target the new subdirectory.

ai.summary: Relocated `agent-config.d.ts` and `tools.d.ts` to `.agents/types/`. Updated imports in `brainstormer.ts`, `charles.ts`, `git-committer.ts`, and `knowledge-keeper.ts`. Made `stepPrompt` optional in `AgentConfig`. Commented out `parentInstructions` in `brainstormer.ts`.

eli5.text: The internal agent configuration files used by the brainstorming and knowledge-keeping assistants were reorganized so that shared definitions live in a more logical folder structure, keeping things tidy for future maintenance. If you looked at the organization, the type definitions for agent settings moved into a dedicated folder, and one optional instruction was commented out so it no longer takes effect. This is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping with no change to how the assistants behave for anyone using them.
